name: M5Stack Unit 4Relay (4x 10 A relays, I2C)
description: M5Stack four-channel relay unit controlled over I2C. An STM32F030F4P6 running M5Stack's firmware at address 0x26 drives four 5 V SPDT relays (TH 932-05VDC-SL-AH type) through SS8050 transistors, with a flyback diode per coil and a programmable red LED per channel. Register 0x10 bit 0 selects LED sync (LEDs follow relays) or manual LEDs; register 0x11 bits 0-3 switch relays 1-4 and bits 4-7 LEDs 1-4. Contacts AC 250 V / DC 28 V, 10 A (16 A peak). Supply 5 V (about 70 mA per energised coil, ~300 mA with all four on); an XC6206 makes 3.3 V for the MCU so SDA/SCL are 3.3 V lines, with no pull-ups on the unit. Sold as: M5Stack Unit 4Relay (SKU U097), Grove HY2.0-4P port GND, 5V, SDA, SCL (black, red, yellow, white), with a 20 cm Grove cable and four HT3.96-4P load terminals.
eli5: A block with four clicky switches inside; your board tells each one to turn a lamp, fan or pump on or off using just two I2C wires.

buildNotes: Power from 5 V (red wire) and share GND. Each energised relay coil draws about 70 mA, so all four on is roughly 300 mA from the 5 V rail; a weak USB port may brown out.
The unit has no I2C pull-ups. On a bare ESP32 or Pico, fit 4.7 kohm from SDA and SCL to 3.3 V (an M5Stack Core already has them).
Address 0x26. Write [0x11, bits] to set relays (bits 0-3 = relays 1-4) and LEDs (bits 4-7); write [0x10, 1] for LEDs that follow the relays. Use read-modify-write to change one relay.
Relay numbering follows M5Stack's Arduino and UiFlow2 libraries (relay n = bit n-1); the docs table lists them in the opposite order, so check which terminal clicks if it matters.
Contacts are rated AC 250 V / DC 28 V, 10 A. Mains wiring is dangerous: keep it in a closed insulated box and leave it to an adult/qualified person. Start with a low-voltage DC load.
Never PWM a relay: it is slow and wears out.

driver.code:
# M5Stack Unit 4Relay (SKU U097), MicroPython driver.
# An STM32F030F4P6 runs M5Stack's firmware at I2C address 0x26 with two byte registers
# (write [reg, value] to set; write [reg] then read 1 byte to get):
#   0x10 mode:  bit 0 = LED sync. 1 = each LED follows its relay, 0 = LEDs set by hand.
#   0x11 state: bits 0-3 = relays 1-4, bits 4-7 = LEDs 1-4 (1 = on).
# Bit numbering follows M5Stack's own Arduino (Unit_4RELAY) and UiFlow2 (relay4.py) libraries.
import time

ADDR = 0x26
REG_MODE = 0x10
REG_STATE = 0x11

MODE_MANUAL = 0  # LEDs controlled independently
MODE_SYNC = 1    # LED n lights while relay n is on


class Unit4Relay:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR, sync=True):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if addr not in i2c.scan():
            raise OSError('Unit 4Relay not found at 0x%02X' % addr)
        # Same start-up as M5Stack's Init(mode): set the mode, then all relays and LEDs off.
        self.set_mode(MODE_SYNC if sync else MODE_MANUAL)
        self._write(REG_STATE, 0x00)

    def _write(self, reg, val):
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # the STM32 firmware needs a short gap between transactions
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([reg, val & 0xFF]))

    def _read(self, reg):
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([reg]))
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 1)[0]

    def set_mode(self, mode):
        self._write(REG_MODE, 1 if mode else 0)

    def mode(self):
        return self._read(REG_MODE) & 0x01

    def state(self):
        """Raw state register: bits 0-3 relays 1-4, bits 4-7 LEDs 1-4."""
        return self._read(REG_STATE)

    def relays(self):
        """Relay bits only (bit 0 = relay 1 ... bit 3 = relay 4)."""
        return self.state() & 0x0F

    def relay(self, n, on=None):
        """relay(n) returns 1/0; relay(n, True/False) switches relay n (1-4)."""
        if not 1 <= n <= 4:
            raise ValueError('relay number must be 1-4')
        bit = 1 << (n - 1)
        s = self.state()
        if on is None:
            return 1 if s & bit else 0
        self._write(REG_STATE, (s | bit) if on else (s & ~bit))

    def led(self, n, on=None):
        """LED n (1-4); only meaningful in manual mode (sync=False)."""
        if not 1 <= n <= 4:
            raise ValueError('LED number must be 1-4')
        bit = 1 << (n + 3)
        s = self.state()
        if on is None:
            return 1 if s & bit else 0
        self._write(REG_STATE, (s | bit) if on else (s & ~bit))

    def all(self, on):
        """All four relays on or off (keeps the LED bits)."""
        s = self.state()
        self._write(REG_STATE, (s | 0x0F) if on else (s & 0xF0))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from unit_4relay import Unit4Relay

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
relays = Unit4Relay(i2c)  # 0x26, LEDs follow relays, all off
while True:
    for n in (1, 3):
        relays.relay(n, True)
        print('RELAY%d ON bits=%04d' % (n, int(bin(relays.relays())[2:])))
        time.sleep(1)
        relays.relay(n, False)
        print('RELAY%d OFF bits=%04d' % (n, int(bin(relays.relays())[2:])))
        time.sleep(1)

# M5Stack Unit 4Relay (U097)

## Overview
Four mechanical relays on one Grove I2C port. An **STM32F030F4P6** running M5Stack's firmware answers at **I2C address 0x26** and drives four **SS8050** transistors, each switching a 5 V relay coil (TH 932-05VDC-SL-AH type, flyback diode across each coil). Each channel also has a red status LED that can follow its relay (sync mode) or be set by hand. An XC6206 regulator makes 3.3 V for the MCU, so SDA/SCL are 3.3 V lines. Hobbyists buy it as the **M5Stack Unit 4Relay (SKU U097)** with a 20 cm Grove cable and four HT3.96-4P plug-in terminals for the contacts.

## Pinout (Grove HY2.0-4P, M5Stack PinMap)
| Pin | Wire | Function |
|---|---|---|
| GND | black | Ground |
| 5V | red | Supply 5 V: relay coils + 3.3 V regulator |
| SDA | yellow | I2C data (3.3 V logic, no pull-up on the unit) |
| SCL | white | I2C clock (3.3 V logic, no pull-up on the unit) |

Load terminals J1-J4 (3.96 mm, one per relay) are on the long edge, so the unit is wired with the Grove cable or jumper leads, not plugged into a breadboard.

## Electrical limits
- Supply 5 V nominal (M5Stack gives no tolerance range; use a regulated 5 V rail such as USB 5 V or an M5Stack Port A). Each energised coil takes roughly 70 mA (0.36 W class 5 V relay), so all four on is about 300 mA from the 5 V rail. 3.3 V will not pull the relays in.
- Contacts: AC 250 V / DC 28 V, 10 A rated, 16 A peak (M5Stack figures).
- I2C pins are STM32 pins at 3.3 V. The unit has **no I2C pull-ups** (an M5Stack Core supplies them); on a bare ESP32/Pico add 4.7 kΩ from SDA and SCL to 3.3 V.

## Interface details
- Address **0x26**. Register write: `[reg, value]`. Register read: write `[reg]`, then read 1 byte.
- `0x10` mode: bit 0 = 1 sync (LED n follows relay n), 0 = manual (LEDs set by hand).
- `0x11` state: bits 0-3 = relays 1-4, bits 4-7 = LEDs 1-4 (1 = on). Change one relay with read-modify-write.
- Bit order follows M5Stack's Arduino `Unit_4RELAY` and UiFlow2 `relay4.py` libraries (relay n = bit n-1). The docs page's register table lists RELAY1 at bit 3; the libraries are what ship, so trust them and check on your unit if the channel number matters.
- M5Stack's drivers wait ~1 ms between transactions; the driver does the same.

## Wiring
- ESP32: GND → GND, 5V → 5V/VIN, SDA → GPIO21, SCL → GPIO22, plus 4.7 kΩ pull-ups SDA/SCL → 3V3.
- M5Stack Core: plug into PORT.A (SDA 21, SCL 22 on Core; 32/33 on Core2).
- Pico: GND → GND, 5V → VBUS, SDA → GP4, SCL → GP5, plus 4.7 kΩ pull-ups to 3V3(OUT).
- Raspberry Pi 4: GND → pin 6, 5V → pin 2, SDA → pin 3, SCL → pin 5 (the Pi has 1.8 kΩ pull-ups).
- Load: supply + → COM, NO → load → supply −.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from unit_4relay import Unit4Relay
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
r = Unit4Relay(i2c)      # 0x26, sync mode, all off
r.relay(1, True)         # relay 1 on (LED 1 follows)
print(r.relays())        # 1 = 0b0001
r.all(False)
```

## Gotchas
- Feed 5 V; four coils together draw about 300 mA, so use a USB supply that can give it.
- No I2C pull-ups on the unit: without a Core or external resistors the bus will not work.
- Mains on the terminals is dangerous: closed insulated box, adult/qualified person only. Start with a low-voltage DC load.
- Relays are slow and wear out: never PWM them.

## Datasheet

Schematic: https://m5stack-doc.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com/589/Sch_UNIT-4RELAY.pdf ·
Libraries: https://github.com/m5stack/M5Unit-RELAY, https://github.com/m5stack/uiflow-micropython/blob/master/m5stack/libs/unit/relay4.py
